title: Article 69 — Oath or affirmation by the Vice-President

content.overview: Article 69 requires every Vice-President to, before entering upon his office, make and subscribe before the President, or some person appointed in that behalf by the President, an oath or affirmation in the form set out in the article (to bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution and faithfully to discharge the duty upon which he is about to enter).
content.glance: VP oath before President (or person appointed by President): true faith and allegiance to the Constitution; faithful discharge of duty.
content.study:
Article 69 oath is taken before the President or a person appointed by the President. The form commits the Vice-President to true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India and to faithful discharge of the duty of the office.

Examination: before whom; substance of oath; contrast Presidential oath (before CJI under Art 60).

sections.heading: Key rule
sections.body: Before entering upon office, the Vice-President makes and subscribes the prescribed oath/affirmation before the President or a person appointed by the President.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Before whom does the Vice-President take the oath?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 69, the Vice-President makes and subscribes the oath or affirmation before the President, or some person appointed in that behalf by the President, before entering upon his office.

examTips: Oath before President; contrast Art 60 (President before CJI).

keyTakeaways: Art 69: VP oath before the President.
